title: The Rotor back to the player's manual override (Isao's auto Rotor could not hit the first wave), the first wave lemon, the hard cores farther out, an enormous arena carved when the world is built, SOL cutting a road ahead of the hull on the drive out, and the one-frame grid flash caught on a screencast but not yet explained
context: Owner, 2026-10-16 (late): 'Start a new planet and then the player has nothing to do for too long, we are stuck in top-down view forever as the rotor apparently fails to hit the first wave entirely... it took 1 full minute, makes no sense. we revert back to user doing the manual override. 1) let's make the first wave yellow-lemon, they are less crazy, slightly bigger target. 2) the purple and black enemies should spawn further away, leaving more time for the player to aim. 3) the grey/blue grid flashing once is still there, maybe the first drawing of something in the background in space?' Then: 'when the tank needs to go to the Arena, have SOL shoot ahead of it here and there to open the maze, making it a cleaner faster road. 2) the ARENA where we land must be MUCH MUCH LARGER, like in the lab... room for the tank to run around and avoid/lure the creatures away, so that SOL and the Gunship can fire... make it an enormous arena.'
outcome: STORY_BEATS.rotorAuto false (the autoTower path stays behind the flag); the first wave is the lemon (STORY_FODDER.type 'ghost', PEARL_OF yellow; story-world hands fodderType to the beats); STORY_QUIVER hold [8, 12] and rise [15, 18] (was 5-9 / 10-13). The Rotor's range 4.6 cells (was 3.6; src/towers.js): the lemons' bodies hold about 42 m off the wall and the piloted Rotor read OUT OF RANGE on all of them (--story-world caught it). THE ARENA IS A PLAIN: ARENA.radiusCells 14; src/domain/arena.js arenaFloor lists every cell within that chord of the arena's cell outside the clearing and src/platform/story-world.js carves them to ground as the world is built (the lab's bound was 12 cells of 10 m; this is a 280 m plain, the maze round it the rim). THE ROAD SOL CUTS: ARENA.road { every 7, ahead 7, burn 2.5, rockCost 4, overhead 45, energy 40, radius 6, slew 16 }; src/domain/arena.js roadAhead (Dial's buckets: the cheapest walk from the hull's cell to the arena with rock at rockCost, the first rock within ahead); on the drive out (the beacon phase) src/fx/boss-run.js asks every `every` seconds and td-tab's solRoad lays a SOL pass over the cell when none is up (laserStation.layPass: the arsenal's pass with nobody seated) and holds the beam on it (aimCell: the harness's own hands), released after `burn`; Isao says arena_road once; nothing while the player sits in SOL or SOL is offline. THE FLASH: a screencast probe (scratchpad flash-probe.mjs: Page.startScreencast plus a per-draw WebGL instrument) catches it every run at the same place, 3.4 s into the landers' tour, one frame, the whole canvas about twice as bright and grey-blue (72, 81, 83) with the planet's far side showing through; in that frame the draw list, the depth mask and the depth test of every draw are identical to the neighbours' (the floor drawn, writing depth), twenty new draws appear (the landers' near tiers), no new program, no console line; the warmer's timer-side one-pixel canvas draw was moved into the frame's tick on suspicion and the flash stayed. Not the breach (opens 2 s earlier), not the reveal (one sector in story mode).
alternatives: Keep the Rotor on auto and tune its aim for the blobs: the owner's call was the manual override; the first wave is now the slower, larger lemon for that seat.
Carve the arena when its sector begins (as the canyon is cut): a plain that stands from the start is simpler for the pathing and the lure's field, and the drive out crosses the maze either way.
Open the road with the MK-9 or the shells: the owner named SOL; its beam already breaks rock by the game's own path.
evidence: test/arena.mjs (the floor by the chord, the road through rock against a detour, the look-ahead), test/story-beats.mjs, test/host-contracts.mjs (57 factories), test/sectors.mjs, npm test and npm run check green
the screencast captures under the session's scratchpad flash/ (frames f08xx with the spike), the draw instrument's draws.json
